title: From a Carry Count to a Carry Recurrence
content: The parent entry (oq-01-oq-01) names carryCount = #{i | pⁱ ≤ (a mod pⁱ) + (b mod pⁱ)} and proves Kummer's theorem vₚ(C(n,k)) = carryCount. That global modular count is correct but never exhibits a carry as something propagated column by column. This follow-up defines the single carry bit carry p m n i = ⌊(m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ)/pⁱ⌋ and the digit dᵢ(x) = ⌊x/pⁱ⌋ mod p, then proves the local schoolbook recurrence that generates the count — the structure Mathlib and the parent both lack.

title: A Carry Is a Single Bit, and How to Peel a Digit
content: Two foundations. carry_le_one: since m mod pⁱ and n mod pⁱ are each below pⁱ, their sum is below 2·pⁱ, so dividing by pⁱ gives 0 or 1 (Nat.div_lt_of_lt_mul) — the carry really is a bit. mod_pow_succ_eq: the identity x mod p^{i+1} = x mod pⁱ + pⁱ·dᵢ(x), which exposes the i-th digit, is exactly Nat.mod_mul applied after pow_succ. These are the two levers the recurrence pulls.

title: The Schoolbook Carry Recurrence (the New Content)
content: carry_succ is the heart of the follow-up: c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) + cᵢ)/p⌋ — the carry out of column i is one exactly when the digit sum plus the incoming carry reaches p. Substituting mod_pow_succ_eq turns the level-(i+1) numerator into pⁱ·(dᵢm + dᵢn) + (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ); because the trailing remainder is below pⁱ, dividing by pⁱ·p (Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul then Nat.mul_add_div) collapses to ⌊(dᵢm + dᵢn + cᵢ)/p⌋, with the incoming carry cᵢ surfacing as ⌊remainder/pⁱ⌋. Neither Mathlib nor the parent entry proves this. carry_eq_zero_of_lt records that carries vanish once pⁱ exceeds m + n.

title: Bridge to Mathlib: Kummer as a Sum of Carry Bits
content: carry_eq_indicator identifies the carry bit with the Boolean indicator of pⁱ ≤ (m mod pⁱ + n mod pⁱ), using Nat.one_le_div_iff and the bit bound. Summing those indicators over Ico 1 b is, by Finset.card_filter, exactly the cardinality counted by padicValNat_choose'. The result padicValNat_choose_eq_sum_carry therefore reads vₚ(C(m+n, m)) = Σ carry bits — the recurrence-based form of the parent's carryCount identity.

title: The Digitwise No-Carry Criterion (Sharpening the Parent)
content: forall_carry_zero_iff runs the recurrence both directions: a vanishing carry c_{i+1} = ⌊(dᵢm + dᵢn)/p⌋ forces dᵢm + dᵢn < p, and conversely all columns below p keep every carry zero by induction. Since carries vanish past the leading digit, the finite condition lifts to all i. With vₚ = Σ carries and vₚ = 0 ⇔ p ∤ C, the corollary not_dvd_choose_iff_no_carry sharpens the parent's carryCount = 0 form to the genuinely digitwise statement: C(m+n, m) is a p-adic unit iff dᵢ(m) + dᵢ(n) < p for every i — adding m and n in base p carries nowhere. At p = 2 this is the classic 'C(m+n, m) is odd iff m and n have disjoint binary supports'.
